### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b68f9ae34734879aee2d57438da3b606f6f97bd7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a506fa70a6cab50004c70ae1f1cddcb32122f043` — the merge of head `b548ddfb97074ff1d2b822f3cd98172789b03acf` into base `b68f9ae34734879aee2d57438da3b606f6f97bd7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a506fa70a6cab50004c70ae1f1cddcb32122f043 && git checkout a506fa70a6cab50004c70ae1f1cddcb32122f043
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b68f9ae34734879aee2d57438da3b606f6f97bd7 b548ddfb97074ff1d2b822f3cd98172789b03acf && git checkout -B drift-repro b68f9ae34734879aee2d57438da3b606f6f97bd7 && git merge --no-ff b548ddfb97074ff1d2b822f3cd98172789b03acf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b68f9ae34734879aee2d57438da3b606f6f97bd7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：脚本里手动开启并已提交或回滚的事务，之后若还有迟到的写入带着它，现在按"不在事务中"正常写入，不再被交给一个已经结束的事务。
- 为什么做：以前这种迟到写入会被塞进已失效的事务连接，跨库时也不会被拦下，行为不可预测；另一种事务写法早已这样处理，这次让两者一致。
- 出错会怎样：只影响事务结束后才到达的写入；事务进行中的写入和跨库拒绝都不变。
- 要你做什么：无。区域审核通过后自行落地。
- 席位意见：改动小而对称，复用已有的"已关闭"判断，证据充分，可以落地。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT** · head `b548ddfb97074ff1d2b822f3cd98172789b03acf` · Fixes #35149 · 2026-11-19T15:22Z · reviewed to `pm-dispatch` text at `origin/main` `fca72dfa32`

Readings, my own: `check-governed-merges --pr 35541` 0 of 5 paths governed; `merge-tree` against main clean; K=14 (<15, no merge owed); CI 37 success / 16 skipped / 0 failed; +133/−12. The claim (7010907655, 13:43Z) predates the 14:38Z p1-only rule, so this p2 is in flight. All files are inside the claimed surface, and `engine.ts` is untouched. The pins are a card-named top-level describe in `engine-transaction-same-origin.test.ts`, the file holding the #35102 pins the claim names, rather than a new file. That keeps one shared harness; no amendment is owed.

**Code.**
- `closeTrioTransactionScope` adds the handle to the `WeakSet` only when `trioTransactionScopes.delete(handle)` returned true. So only a handle the trio itself opened can be marked closed, and a foreign handle is left as it was.
- `recordTrioTransactionScope` clears the mark, so a driver that reuses the handle object reads as open again.
- `isClosedUnitHandle` consults the trio mark only when `openedUnits` has no entry. A `transaction()` unit's own verdict is unchanged, and a detached handle still short-circuits first.
- The import is one-way (`engine-transactions-section` → `engine-execute-transactions`, which imports neither the section nor `unit-detach`), so no cycle is added.

Every reader of `isClosedUnitHandle` treats "closed" as absent and falls back to the ambient transaction or none, never to a refusal. I checked `driverOptions`, the cross-datasource write check, secret-field release, `writeTransactionOf`/summaries, `opensAfterAbortUnit` and `openTransactionKind`. So a closed trio handle now gets exactly the closed-unit treatment from #22855.

**Pins (names grepped).**
- The two #35102 cells are renamed to `treats the handle as closed once the trio commits / rolls back` and now also assert the late write carries no transaction.
- The new describe `a trio handle closes as a transaction() unit handle does (#35149)` has five cells:
  - parity of the late cross-datasource write against a closed unit handle;
  - the late same-datasource write runs unenrolled, never on the dead handle;
  - CONTROL: an open trio handle still enrolls, and a cross-datasource write under it is still refused `ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE`;
  - body-door parity, `separate` while open and `none` once committed;
  - the reused handle reads as open on its next begin.
- A0 (late ledger insert handed the dead primary handle), the two ablations (7 red, 1 red) and the objectql suite (13900 passed) are from os-dev-report 7012990620.

**Declaration: agreed.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` / `@objectstack/objectql` patch. No accepted input gains a refusal: the cross-datasource refusal still fires only under an open handle, and the late write now succeeds unenrolled where it was handed a dead handle. `openTransactionKind` moves from `'separate'` to `'none'` for a closed trio handle, within its existing union. That is the correct answer for a finished transaction, and the body doors then pass no dead handle. The changeset states it. No L2 is owed.

**Gates.** 5 dist-reading gates and `check:type-check-debt` were not run locally (the lock was busy); CI's green covers them on this head.

**Routing.** Not governed and no contract face: data-1 lands it.
